reason: Legal on every hard rule and it is the one chapter the spec forbids inventing a venue for (R9: 'the plate is a street of those seven premises'). Venue type named first, place_category 'village shop row' is three lowercase words and matches the place text, anchor is inanimate and cuts lower-left to upper-right, and the activity ('taking in the morning delivery') is a real verb 18 people can each be seen performing at their own doorway. All seven required SCENE_TOKENs get an explicit, architecturally-scaled hosting line — colliery gates, weaving workshop, police box, five-storey hotel, club side door with the horseshoe magnet, dairy, mynah over the seed merchant — and the delivery round supplies release/reuptake as native trade action rather than metaphor, which is the R5 requirement met without invention. 'MESSENGER ROW' is 2 words, reads as an ordinary street nameplate and does not print the topic word. Two conditions on the redraw: (a) the pit gate must stay a closing element at the head of the road, not the subject, or the plate starts reading as ch4's mine; (b) 7 tokens + 16 stock props is at the top of the density budget at 1376x768 — cap required lettered strings at 8 per §9.

Strongest venue in the batch. DOPA + MINE is a true morpheme split landing on a real place-noun, and numbered pithead boards are authentic signage, so the sign reads as a real place. Four hand-boarded gallery mouths off one shaft is a genuine spatial isomorphism for four tracts leaving one cell-body region, and the venue is soaked in the fixed lexicon token rope = dopamine (winding rope, drum, loose ends) at zero extra cost — the best R9 integration anyone has proposed here. Anchor (inclined haulage way with rails and standing tubs) is inanimate and diagonal with the headframe over it. Props are authentic colliery stock (lamp checks, tubs, canary, pit props, safety lamp, tally board), not filler. CONDITIONS: (i) 'No.4' on the pithead board reads as the pit's NAME, not a count — §3 explicitly rejects a carrier whose native numeric meaning competes with the intended one (a milepost reading 5 reads as distance). Keep the board, but let the four boarded gallery mouths carry the count as a COUNTED_SET, which is the corpus route for small integers anyway. (ii) Letter the four gallery boards with what each gallery is digging so the tracts are individually addressable; four identical holes are one fact, not four.

The hosting of the chapter's single most important token is physically incoherent. `place` says 'lock-up stalls down both sides' of 'one long central aisle', and the anchor is that aisle; but stock_props and hosts_tokens then put 'a rug stall with a loom running the length of the central aisle' with 'the loom set on the floor seam'. A loom occupying the full length of the aisle contradicts the stall layout, blocks the declared activity (shoppers 'working down the aisle with a basket'), and breaks the one-perspective/physically-coherent rule. Secondary: structurally this is ch3 again in the same batch — a run of small trading units, one per token, with the RAPHE weaving unit on the midline and a postal-delivery reuptake worker. ch3 is spec-mandated, so ch5 is the one that has to differentiate. The acronym itself ('5 HIGH TOWN' = 5-H-T as word initials) and the TAROT_2A hosting (curtained booth with the pie stall = 2C, wash-down channels = 3, book stall = 6 opening off it) are genuinely good and worth keeping.
better_alternative: Keep the covered market hall, rebuild the layout as a real market-hall CENTRAL ISLAND: one long narrow island lock-up on the hall's midline is the raphe rug workshop (it literally sits on the seam and ships rolled rugs out to every counter in the building), with a walking aisle down each side and the perimeter runs on both outer walls. Anchor becomes 'the central island run and its floor seam, corner to corner'; the shopping activity is then unobstructed and the raphe's ship-everywhere geometry is stronger, not weaker. Push the tarot booth, the all-night kiosk and the bus-stop booth to the corner arches as now, and move the postman to the island's own delivery end so SERT collects from the seam. Differentiate from ch3 by trade register: ch3 is the delivery-in morning, ch5 is the customer's mid-morning shop.

reason: A travelling circus is a spectacle venue, and three separate failures follow from having picked it to hold three tokens at once rather than for the pun. (1) The declared activity is 'putting the tent up', but BEETHOVEN_ORCHESTRA is hosted as a seated band on a rostrum with drums, brass and winds and a conductor on the box — a full band cannot be raising canvas, so the token and the one-shared-activity rule (R4) contradict each other. (2) ALPHA_WOLF_PACK is placed loose on open ground 'between the trees and the horse lines'. Loose wolves beside a picketed horse line is not a physically coherent showground; a circus wolf act travels in a cage wagon. (3) A blue police box is street furniture on a town pavement; it does not stand at the gate of a field a travelling show pitched in last night, so LOCUS_COERULEUS_BLUEPOST is bolted on. Also near-duplicates the existing county-fair midway world (ch89) and the promenade amusement family. 'NOR'EAST' as the NOR- morpheme plus the fixed N-compass is the one part that works.
better_alternative: A municipal park bandstand on a frosty Sunday — place_category 'park bandstand'. Every token becomes native instead of imported: the bandstand rostrum IS Beethoven's stand (heart-drums one side, brass and winds the other, the fishing NET hung on the stand's stair by the park keeper); a blue police box stands at the park gates, which is exactly where police boxes stood; and the park's snowy pine belt runs behind the railings with the numbered-collar pack out on the frosted grass beyond the deer fence and the keeper's dart rifle in the fence hut — a fenced enclosure inside a Victorian park, which is not the zoo category. Anchor: the bandstand's raked steps and the iron park railing cutting the frame on a diagonal. Activity: everyone is turning out for the band concert — carrying and setting the folding chairs in rows, tuning, taking a seat, passing the collection tin. Sign 'NOR'EAST PARK BAND' (3 words). Mundane, unique, and the tent-raising/band contradiction disappears.

reason: Accepted only on the pun and on the hard condition below. 'Nursery' is a true homonym needing zero distortion, the sign reads as a real garden centre, the anchor (long potting bench under the tunnel hoops) is inanimate and diagonal, and HARDENING OFF on a cold frame is a genuinely native carrier for separation. But as written the venue contains NO CHILDREN: the stated activity is 'staff and customers potting seedlings on', and all sixteen props are horticultural, so every aspect lands on a pot or a tray. 'Rows of identical pots side by side but never touching = parallel play' is precisely the banned move — pots do not play, and §5 caps FREE_METAPHOR at <=5% and forbids minting fresh metaphors for behavioural states when a person can simply exhibit them. As written this plate would be ~80% free metaphor. CONDITION (hard, and it saves the venue rather than replacing it): re-specify the activity as a CHILDREN'S SATURDAY POTTING WORKSHOP at the garden centre — families at the bench, every child potting their own bean. Then parallel play is two children at the same bench each potting alone without cooperating; vocabulary is a child reading names off the pencil labels; fine motor is children on the scissors and trowel; magical thinking is a child talking to the scarecrow (already in the prop list, currently unassigned); separation is a child clinging at the tunnel door beside the HARDENING OFF frame. The plants revert to what they should have been all along — the venue's free stock inventory, not the fact carriers.

'School' is a true homonym doing double duty: the shoal turning as one IS peer conformity, so the pun and the fact are the same object. The class visit correctly puts real children in the frame with a shared native activity (touring and filling in the worksheet), 'NO TAPPING THE GLASS' screwed to the wall is a textbook RULE_ON_A_SIGN for moral development, and the anchor (curved acrylic tunnel driving lower-left to upper-right with the lit tanks banked along it) is inanimate and diagonal. Props are authentic aquarium stock. CONDITIONS: (i) The sign is the weak link. 'Old school' is a fixed English idiom meaning retro/traditional, so the strongest reading of the sign actively misdirects away from school age. Same length, same pun, no false reading: 'SCHOOL DAYS AQUARIUM'. (ii) Peer rejection and self-concept must move onto the visiting children, not the fish: the rejected child is a child standing apart from the class, and self-concept is a child studying their own reflection in the tank glass. Delete 'mirror panel a fish keeps butting' outright — the mirror self-recognition test is chapter 8's device (its full-length mirror), and running it again here cross-contaminates two adjacent chapters.

After chapter 4, the strongest entry. 'Attachments' is a true homonym — the shop literally sells attachments — and 'Bowlby & Sons' is simultaneously the eponym and the single most ordinary hardware-shop form there is; printing a theorist's name is legal (the ban is on diagnoses, and Lithium Lift prints its drug outright). The four carded fittings (SECURE FIT / AVOIDS DUST / CLINGS ON / TANGLES) are a correct R7 prop family: four siblings from one parent key differing in one attribute, the four-travel-posters device. 'WE FIND WHAT'S INSIDE' hand-lettered over a repairman with his ear against a machine's casing is the best encoding of mentalization proposed anywhere in this batch — it is the shop's real service, not a metaphor. Anchor (repair counter backed the full length by the pegboard wall) is inanimate and diagonal. CONDITIONS: (i) The Strange Situation is the actual exam content and currently gets one line ('a child left with a toy trolley'). Build it out as a bounded pair on native stock: a child at the far end of an extended vacuum hose with the parent at the counter (secure base plus exploration), and the child's state at the moment the parent steps to the pavement. Keep it as one pairwise relation, not a story arc. (ii) De-Anglicise to a hardware store; the pegboard, drawers, key cutter and repair counter all survive unchanged. (iii) 'Carabiners and a safety harness on a hook' duplicates the secure-base slot already held by the dog lead — differentiate or cut, per the cue-distinctiveness triple.

PERSONAL is the morpheme on a name a real tattoo studio could carry, and the ink is not a freshly minted metaphor for a clinical state - it is a CONTRAST_PAIR built out of the shop's own stock (henna/wash-off counter by the window vs the permanent chairs at the back), which section 5 lists as a sanctioned extension. Three lettered flash cabinets A/B/C each in its own house style is R7 sibling-prop-family encoding done properly: three facts off one piece of furniture, differentiated by instance rather than by swapping families. 'MUST BE 18+' is a door sticker whose native job is exactly the not-before-18 convention, and the laser-removal price list carries slow, partial, expensive change without a word of clinical text. Anchor (flash wall + trolley rail) is inanimate and diagonal. REQUIRED FIXES: (a) density - three booths and a bench will not carry R6's 12-25 comparable-scale figures and the frame will fail check_composition's 'filled to all four edges'; stage it as a Saturday walk-in with a full waiting bench, a second artist's row and people at the flash wall choosing; (b) the laser price list is your only digit carrier - if you paint a figure, tag it on the same card, otherwise leave it as squiggle; (c) put ink on the artists and the counter staff too, so the plate does not read as the claim 'personality disorder = the tattooed ones'.

Not mood-matched - bright flat noon light, ordinary municipal shift - and not a minted metaphor: 'affect is the weather, mood is the climate' is the MSE's own teaching definition, so this is LITERAL_PICTURE of the definition, the same status as depression = a hollow in the ground. The barograph is the best single element in the batch for its aspect: an instantaneous needle reading beside a week-long ink trace on one bench IS cross-sectional vs longitudinal with nothing invented, and the max/min thermometer is an instrument whose only job is recording a range. 'EUTHYMIC FALLS' is legal by the Chateau Tyramine precedent - a clinical word wrapped in a real place-noun, not a diagnosis on a sign. Anchor (Stevenson screen + guyed anemometer mast) is inanimate and slices the frame. REQUIRED FIXES, and this one is 'workable' for a reason: (1) DENSITY IS THE BLOCKER - a met station is a one-or-two-person job and R6 demands 12-25 figures sharing one activity; restage it explicitly as a trainee-observer training day or an inspection round so fifteen people are plausibly walking the same hourly round, otherwise the composition gate fails on figure count. (2) The largest lettering slot currently goes to the venue name, which violates DON'T #1; promote a short painted board ('READINGS ON THE HOUR' or 'CLIMATE EXPECTED - WEATHER GIVEN', 4 words) to the biggest string. (3) Congruence is specified as one confused observer, which is unaddressable; make it a bounded pairwise relation - the observer's logged sheet vs the instrument he is standing at - so the legend can cue it as a prop pair.

PHARM/FARM is a genuine double pun on a name that reads as an ordinary rural address, and the venue's population is children, so 'pediatric' is carried by the place itself and never has to be labelled. Largest string is 'START LOW - GO SLOW', i.e. the doctrine and not the name, exactly as DON'T #1 requires. The black flag in a rack beside the yellow and the chequered is the find of this entry: a track's flags already ARE a graded colour-coded safety language, so the black-box warning arrives with zero invention and inherits a real-world hierarchy. Weigh-in scale = mg/kg, height gauge = size limit, restrictor plate = titration, peeled sponsor decal + 'NO LABEL' = off-label are all native stock, not filler. Anchor (tyre wall + gantry) is inanimate and diagonal, and it splits the frame into grid, circuit, pit lane and paddock. REQUIRED FIXES: (a) 'PIT EVERY 3 LAPS' and the brass weigh-in weights are two competing digit carriers whose native units (laps, kilograms) both compete with the fact - keep one, tag it, drop the other to the legend; MAX_PAINTED_NUMBERS is 3 and 0 is legal. (b) CROSS-CHAPTER COLLISION: tarmac, cones, barriers, queued vehicles and an official with a clipboard is visually the same page as chapter 21's driving-test yard. It survives the letter of the phase rule (phase 1 vs 2) but they are five chapters apart in study order and will interfere. I am rejecting 21 on independent grounds; if 21 is instead kept as written, this venue must move.

The required SCENE_TOKEN cannot be hosted at a readable scale. DOPA_MINE is a course-wide fixed structure with four labelled pathway chambers, coal carts, the red D2 barrier, the up-elevators, the EXTRA pyramid hats and the DAT figure gathering ore back; this venue compresses all of it into one glass-cased penny-in-the-slot automaton against a side wall. In a 1376x768 frame carrying 22+ elements that cabinet is roughly a tenth of the frame width, so the four labelled chambers are unreadable — and §9 names resolution as the binding constraint that must be decided, not noted. Worse, it demotes a fixed course-wide structure to a miniature ornament: R9's rule is that a venue which cannot host the token is rejected, not the token. Secondary: an indoor seafront coin-amusement hall sits very close to the surviving promenade prize-shooting gallery (ch101) — same trade family, same furniture (shutter front, prize shelf above head height, coin counter, kick rail, queue for the next go). The fascia ('Hyper' as one morpheme, a name real arcades trade under) and the criteria carriers (minimum-token notice, accompanied-under-twelves door notice, branch board for the second setting, ticket tallies for the rating scales) are the strongest part and should be carried across.
better_alternative: Move ADHD onto the pit road so the mine can stand at architectural scale, exactly as ch3 does, and declare adjacent_to [4]: a coal merchant's bagging yard and weighbridge at the foot of the colliery road — place_category 'coal merchant's yard'. Activity: everyone is making up the round — shovelling and weighing a bag on the platform scale, stitching the neck, swinging it onto the lorry, and taking the weigh-ticket. The colliery gates and winding gear close the head of the yard full size with the four labelled gallery mouths in the gate yard. The criteria then ride on carriers whose real job is to bear them, keeping every device from the arcade version: the weigh-ticket spike = rating scales, the round board listing two delivery rounds = symptoms in two settings, the six-bag standard load chalked on the board = the symptom threshold, the date stamp on the ticket = age-of-onset before 12, and the minimum-load notice on the office window = the impairment threshold. Sign 'HYPERDRIVE HAULAGE' or 'HYPER FUELS'.

reason: AMPHI- carries amphetamine and the venue then ships a whole WALL of stencilled AMP cabinets - the class morpheme repeated as ordinary equipment, which is R7 sibling-family encoding at its best (four sibling travel posters = four SSRIs). The marquee spends the largest string on 'CONCERTA - 12 HOUR SHOW', so the biggest lettering carries the extended-release duration rather than the name (DON'T #1, correct). The adder lying in the snake cables is a real gig noun carrying Adderall; the follow-spot's FOCUS ring is real hardware carrying Focalin; the food truck with no queue is LITERAL_DEPICTION of appetite suppression; the VU meter pinned in the red is a dial whose native job is showing something running hot; and the scalper at the fence is the exact pharmacological word 'diversion' rendered as a picture rather than a metaphor. Anchor (scaffold tower + crowd barrier) is inanimate, diagonal, and yields four real zones. WATCH ITEMS: (a) mood-congruence hazard - a loud concert for a stimulant class is the one venue here that could drift into atmosphere-picking; the entry defends itself by specifying doors-open on a summer afternoon during load-in, and that MUST be enforced at render (flat daylight, crew humping flight cases, no night-time light show), or it becomes the failure the spec is fixing. (b) 'Twin decks' -> Dexedrine is the weakest of the four agent puns; strengthen to a road case stencilled 'DEX' or the right-hand deck labelled 'DEXTER'. (c) Tag the 12 ('12 HR') and hold total painted numerals to 3. (d) Your crowd barrier is the same object on the same diagonal as chapter 21's crash barrier in the same phase - resolved by 21 moving.

The strongest derivation in the batch: the class's mechanism is performed as the venue's ordinary work rather than illustrated. Calling the dog off the flock IS the alpha-2 autoreceptor, the sheep netting IS the NET transporter drawn as the object it is named after, the all-day gather carries atomoxetine's delayed onset, the gatepost hazard notice carries clonidine rebound, and letting a batch off the pressure at once is how a flock genuinely bolts. 'CLONMEL' is a real Irish town name carrying the clon- morpheme, 3 words, nothing clinical printed. Category is distinct from the surviving ploughing match (ch114) and pick-your-own (ch46); activity is a real verb a whole hill's worth of people can each be seen doing. Two mandatory fixes before it ships. (1) The contract is currently self-contradictory about which prop carries alpha-2: pun_explanation says 'the second collie, tagged and hanging back on the skyline, is the pack token', while hosts_tokens says the tagged wolves on the plantation edge are. That is exactly the fact-to-element ambiguity §1 identifies as the root defect — delete the collie claim and let the tagged wolves be the sole carrier. (2) Having declared that, differentiate the instance per R7 so the two canid families cannot be confused: working collies black-and-white and in motion below the fence, wolves grey, numbered-collared and static behind the deer fence at the treeline.

Legal PHONETIC_PUN (AUTO- = autos/self) on a genuine, wholly mundane eating hall, and the automat's real business model is criterion A: you take your meal from a wall of machines, there is no server, there is nobody to reciprocate with. That is isomorphism from the trade, not atmosphere — it passes the test a lesser author fails by picking an empty place to mood-match isolation. Criterion B then comes free off the same furniture (grid of identical windows, cutlery aligned in parallel, spun coin, tokens in a strict row, 'PLEASE - QUIET' under a buzzing tube). REQUIRED FIXES: (a) place_category is missing — declare 'automat cafeteria'; this is the field the global dedup runs on, and its absence is why ch1 and ch115 both shipped as high-street opticians. (b) COMPETING CARRIER, §3: coin slots stamped '18' and '24' read as coin denominations, not months — a changer booth is the worst possible carrier for an age in months; move screening ages to a wall calendar or the notice board. (c) The venue-level paint budget is already blown at four strings ('1 2 3', '18', '24', '1 IN 36') against MAX_PAINTED_NUMBERS = 3 — triage before the element table is built. (d) Neither required token is hostable as written: `asd` is a whole train-workshop scene and `DSM_neurodevelopmental` is a six-corner classroom. The automat already contains the reduced form — a child on the tiled floor laying automat tokens in a strict line — so declare it in hosts_tokens instead of leaving the token unmet. (e) Period venue: hold the bright register, no sepia nostalgia drift.

Legal acronym embed — I, D, D contiguous inside KIDD, which reads as an ordinary English family firm and never prints the diagnosis. place_category 'ladder works' is a real trade, is unique across all 144, and is nowhere near the taken list. The severity mapping is corpus-sanctioned rather than invented: graded ability as height on four ladders against one wall is §3 rule 10 (continuous gradients are vertical position, p143's dose axis), and the amount of weight the person footing the stile takes is the support-level criterion shown as work, not as a metaphor for a mental state — no §5 ban is touched, and nobody in the frame 'is' the disability. Three-section extension ladder for before/during/after and three racked bays for the three domains are free slots the trade already owns. Two weaknesses to fix rather than reasons to reject: hosts_tokens is empty although symbols_needed lists idd and DSM_neurodevelopmental, so add explicit hosting lines (the visual schedule of photographs and the chunky-grip aids belong on the yard notice board and the bench; the ND-family corners can ride the three racked bays); and four test ladders cannot support 18 people all 'working the test wall', so widen the wall to eight or nine ladders or state that the rest are tagging, racking and gluing rungs under the canopy.

Corpus-quality LITERAL_PICTURE. LEXI is the live morpheme of dyslexia on a name any jobbing printer could carry, and letterpress is the one ordinary trade where type genuinely IS mirror-reversed and where b, d, p and q genuinely do get returned to the wrong compartment — 'MIND YOUR P's AND Q's' is a real typesetters' idiom that exists for exactly that reason. Three specifiers on three real benches with nothing invented, and '6 MONTHS OF PROOFS' is a native duration carrier. REQUIRED FIXES: (a) place_category missing — declare 'letterpress print shop'. (b) TWO ANCHORS declared (platen press AND composing bench 'running together'); R3 wants one structure that is the largest thing in frame — pick the bench run and demote the press. (c) CLINICAL ACCURACY: letter reversal is a popular misconception, not a DSM-5-TR criterion; the legend rows must read decoding/fluency/accuracy, or the plate teaches the myth. The venue survives this because in letterpress the reversal is literally true of the type, not of the child. (d) The chapter's stated central differential — SLD vs IDD, normal ability in other domains — has no carrier; the lexicon's own `sld` token supplies it (the accurate model rocket on the same desk), so host it as a flawless wood-engraving pinned above the blotted practice sheet. (e) The ink/print sector is crowded (ch44 EXPOSURE PRINTS photo lab, ch14 PERSONAL INK tattoo parlour); distinct trades, but declare adjacent_to so three shops do not blur into one world.

Near-duplicate of two surviving venues, and the duplication is at the level of activity and props, not just category. ch43 (OCEAN DAILY CATCH, wet fish shop) is already 'pulling a numbered ticket, pointing at the row, weighing on the hanging dial, wrapping in paper' over a chilled slab with a hose and a numbered ticket queue; ch31 (MAYO'S AGED DELI) is already 'taking a ticket, waiting, pointing at the case, being handed wrapped parcels' over a long glass counter. This butcher is the third instance of the identical world — glass counter of cold cuts, take-a-ticket queue, hanging scale, wrapping-paper spindle, sawdust floor, price board. That is the six-launderettes failure the global dedup rule exists to stop: the chapter name will not retrieve a single unique world. Secondary: hosts_tokens is empty although communication_disorders and DSM_neurodevelopmental are required, and the four subtypes are asserted in the pun_explanation rather than given hosting lines. The fascia itself is excellent — keep 'tongue' on the sign.
better_alternative: TONGUE & GROOVE — a flooring and joinery mill, place_category 'joinery mill'. Tongue-and-groove is a genuine trade term and a name real joiners trade under, so the organ of articulation is still lettered on the fascia inside a trade with nothing to do with speech, and the world is unique across the 144. Activity: everyone is matching boards — feeding a board through the moulder, offering the tongue into the next board's groove, tapping it home, and stacking the run. All four subtypes then become native shop-floor business instead of restated clinical vignettes: boards whose tongue will not enter the groove at all = language disorder; boards machined to the wrong profile so the joint sits proud = speech sound disorder; the moulder that judders and repeats the same cut on one board = stuttering; and the mill's own posted feed-order rule (one man feeds, one man takes off, wait your turn at the outfeed) with the worker who keeps grabbing out of turn = social-pragmatic. The mirror move survives as the setting-out mirror over the outfeed table.

reason: Best derivation of the twelve. TIC = TICK and TOURETTE = TURRET, 'turret clock' is the genuine horological trade term, so one three-word shop sign carries both halves of the chapter title in ordinary trade language with no clinical word on it. The venue then does the diagnosis unaided: a turret clock both ticks and strikes, so motor tics are the escapement and vocal tics are the bell and hammer, and Tourette's both-required rule is a CONTRAST_PAIR against the tick-only wall clocks and the chime-only case. The WARNING WHEEL is the find of the batch — the real horological name for the run that engages just before the strike, so the premonitory urge arrives with zero invention and with a hand hovering over it as the bounded relation. REQUIRED FIXES: (a) COMPETING CARRIER, §3: a clock face standing between 10 and 12 for peak age reads as o'clock, never as years, and it also duplicates the '12 MONTHS' ticket rack, which paint-string uniqueness forbids; move peak age to an apprentice indenture board or drop it to the legend. (b) DENSITY: a repair works employs five men, not R6's 12-25 figures; stage the tower's annual service or an open day with visitors on the stair and a queue at the counter. (c) place_category missing — declare 'clock repair works'; note ch19 was rejected partly for duplicating this interior, so this chapter is the category holder and the two amber alpha-2 pilot lamps must be preserved verbatim wherever ch19 relands (R9 one-way door). (d) The 'S | F' regulator lever is unassigned to any fact and will pollute the TEXT gate — assign or cut.

Conditional, and the condition is not optional. What earns the accept: the ambient activity IS the stereotypy — the same two-handed crate flick repeated by everyone down the whole run of bins — rather than a picture of it, and the stylus stuck in a locked groove is a stock object whose native malfunction is the diagnosis. That is the p199 'customers lying down to try beds' device and it is the rarest thing in this batch. What is broken: DCD, half the chapter, rides entirely on 'tangled patch-cable loom = motor planning', a freshly minted metaphor for a clinical state, which §5 bans outright (0 of 113 corpus items), propped up by an obscure text pun (PRAXIS is a defunct experimental record label; no psychiatry resident reads that crate divider). The legal move is already in the shop: LITERAL_DEPICTION at 41% corpus share — a customer who cannot get the stylus down on the groove, drops the sleeve, mis-files it, knocks a crate over; keep PRAXIS only as the printed morpheme and demote the cable loom to filler. Also: place_category missing — declare 'second-hand record shop'. Also: the sign carries nearly the whole root ('stereo type' vs 'stereotypic'), which is the closest thing in this batch to the banned MAJOR DEPRESSION QUARRY, so no legend row may spell the diagnosis in Latin next to it. Finally, ch19 (music shop) and ch24 (clock repair works) are two more narrow specialist shops with a back repair bench — differentiate this one as a bright wide shop floor or declare the adjacency.

The best number/string work in the batch, and none of it is invented: 'FRAGILE' and 'XL' are pre-printed on real egg-station stock before the illustrator arrives, which is the Chateau Tyramine device done properly, and the candling lamp is the trade's own radiograph, so a three-yolk egg is a legal COUNTED_SET for trisomy and two bubbles on the same candling screen is the double-bubble sign on a native carrier. Lot stamp and numbered size lane are carriers whose real job is to bear digits (§3 stage 3). 'DOWNS FARM EGGS' is 3 words, reads as an ordinary landscape farm name, and prints one morpheme, not the diagnosis — the licensed MAJOR PIT move. Activity is a real verb a whole shift can each be seen doing; venue type named first; place_category matches; anchor inanimate and diagonal; day shift with the door open keeps the register flat per R8. Distinct enough from the surviving canning works (ch120) and glass packers (ch127) because the candling booth and grading lanes give it a silhouette neither has. Two conditions: declare adjacent_to 127, because the FRAGILE stencil is load-bearing in both and both are FMR1 chapters — undeclared, that reads as an accidental collision rather than a shared universe; and add a hosting line for DSM_neurodevelopmental instead of leaving hosts_tokens empty.

Near-duplicate of #38 in this same batch. Both are trade-counter supply premises and their declared anchors are literally the same object: a floor-to-roof steel racking run of boxed trade stock crossing lower-left to upper-right, splitting the room into counter / test bench / stock wall / doorway. Both have a sign-out book on the counter (docket pad vs issue book), a bench where stock is triggered or sounded to prove it works, stock hanging on wall hooks, dated inspection labels on every item (test-and-tag expiry vs dated service tags) and graded sizes on a pegboard or size chart. Two chapters studied days apart would retrieve the same room. Of the pair this is the one that must move, because its strength is the phonetic pun and the pun is trade-independent: rent-a-X works on any hire business, whereas #38's one-hazard-per-bay isomorphism only exists in that specific shop. The venue's native logic inverts the diagnosis it was chosen for. A seed bank's constitutional purpose is that nothing is ever discarded and duplicates are deliberately retained — that behaviour is correct, funded, catalogued and institutionally sanctioned there. Hoarding Disorder's diagnostic core is difficulty discarding PLUS accumulation that congests and clutters active living areas so they cannot be used for their intended purpose, PLUS distress and impairment. The seed bank scores zero on the last two natively, which is why the author has to bolt on a corridor narrowed to one walking width and a fire door held shut by crates — fixtures a real accessions hall would never tolerate, i.e. invented props dressed as stock, exactly what the stock-inventory rule exists to prevent. A venue where the diagnosis is best practice teaches that the diagnosis is best practice. Second failure: it is not a cliche real-world place. The free-slot economy only pays out if the learner already owns the object; an accession register, a ruled counting board, a camel-hair brush and brass calipers closed on one grain are specialist objects nobody in the target audience can picture, so the 'large stock inventory of ordinary objects' is a large inventory of unfamiliar ones. Third: BDD is the chapter's first-named disorder and gets nothing on the sign and nothing literal in the frame. 'A grader rejects a specimen for a flaw nobody else can see' is the STRUCTURE of BDD transposed onto an external object — a FREE_METAPHOR, which §5 caps at 5% and explicitly bans for clinical states, where the only three legal moves are a person literally exhibiting it, a fixed token, or a famous artwork. The mirror by the coat hooks is the sole literal BDD prop and it is filler-grade. The muscle-dysmorphia specifier drawn as a broad-shouldered grader choosing the plumpest grains is a pun on seed plumpness, not on the specifier. Fourth, minor: germination trays under a lamp and racks of graded seed converge with ch9 LITTLE SPROUTS and ch32 THYME & AGAIN, and the jarred-grain silhouette converges with ch124 MY GRAIN & FEED.

The clinical reasoning this venue encodes is genuinely superb — dating damage by how far it has aged is bruise dating, separating damage inherent to the object from damage inflicted on it is the whole mimics differential, the x-ray box is the skeletal survey, the dated report filed whether or not anyone asked is the reporting duty, and the picture back for the fourth time with fresh damage and a new account is Factitious Disorder Imposed on Another. That machinery is worth rescuing. The venue is not. Three failures. Eighteen conservators swinging raking lamps in one room is not a real place, and the declared activity — examining a work and writing down what you find — is quiet, solitary and slow, which is the opposite of a packed frame. (2) It is not a cliche premises. The rule is explicit that the venue must carry a large stock of ORDINARY objects because each one is a free fact-slot, and a free slot only pays out if the learner already owns the object.
